rationale.conceptual: The method is the paper's own custom micromechanics modeling with multiple interacting components (thermal expansions, mechanical expansions, continuity equations, and boundary conditions). Translating the mathematical formulation (40-56 unknowns per cell) into a correct global linear system requires genuine understanding of the substructuring and handling of interior/boundary cells, making it a non-trivial implementation. It is not a standard algorithm but a specific multi-part derivation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of ~6 sequential stages (define geometry, compute continuum baseline, conduct thermal analysis, mechanical analysis, extract resultants, export stress profiles) with dependencies. It does not require external tooling beyond standard Python libraries, and the I/O is straightforward CSV output, but assembling the correct global matrices for varying M adds complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a detailed higher-order micromechanical theory from scratch, involving thermal and mechanical analysis with quadratic expansions, assembly of large linear systems from continuity conditions, and computation of normalized resultants. The method is not a simple library call; it demands understanding of the substructuring and many governing equations. The execution pipeline has about 6 stages with matrix assembly and linear solves, but remains CPU-only and low-resource.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The largest linear system size is 56×M unknowns (M≤20), so matrices are tiny (<10 MB memory). All parameters are hard-coded, no external data required. CPU-only execution suffices.
